transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-18 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samira (Redwood SE), Priya (Solstice Eng Lead), Miguel (Solstice CTO), Alex (Solstice Backend)

Summary: Quickstart and hands-on walkthrough for Redwood SDKs (Python + TypeScript), environment bootstrapping (sandbox, CI secrets), auth patterns (API keys, SSO/SAML, KMS), and Optimize recommendations (batching, KV cache, quantization suggestions). Agreed to provision a sandbox, run a small benchmark, and share security/compliance docs.

Topics: SDK quickstart, API key rotation, CI integration, sandbox invite, dedicated vs hosted discussion, private deployment concerns (VPC/KMS), Optimize suggestions for latency/cost tradeoffs, next steps and pilot plan.

00:00 Jordan: okay hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll keep this hands-on. I'm Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE here, with Samira who is our solutions engineer.
00:12 Samira: hi all, quick intro, i'll take the demo and then we can drop into the SDKs. if anything's fuzzy shout out.
00:20 Priya: thanks, yeah excited — we want to get devs unblocked. main asks: auth patterns for CI and rotating keys, and also how to keep PII inside our VPC for HIPAA compliance.
00:34 Jordan: great, that maps well to what we planned. Samira, can you pull up the console?
00:40 Samira: sure pulling the sandbox console, um the first thing you'll see is Projects -> we usually create a sandbox org for POCs. i'll create a project called solstice-poc-demo.
00:55 Alex: quick question — for api keys, do you recommend storing them in our existing secrets manager or using Redwood-managed keys?
01:03 Samira: good q. for rapid evals we generate API keys from the console and store them in your CI secrets (GH Actions/Bitbucket). for production we recommend KMS integration and bringing your own key for encrypted storage of secrets. you can also enable key rotation via our API.
01:20 Miguel: is there an HSM option or customer-managed key? our security team insists.
01:25 Samira: yes, BYOK via KMS/HSM is supported in Private and Dedicated deployments; hosted supports envelope encryption with customer KMS via IAM roles. i'll note that and we'll include the KMS integration guide in the packet.
01:40 Priya: about SSO — we'd like SAML so our engineers don't need separate logins.
01:44 Jordan: SAML/SSO and SCIM provisioning are available on enterprise plans — works with Okta/Azure AD. we'll include a SAML setup step and a runbook.

02:05 Samira: demo time — SDK quickstart. i'll do Python first, then TypeScript. starting with pip install redwood-client (note: package name may differ in recording) then init with REDWOOD_API_KEY env var.
02:20 Samira: code snippet: from redwood import RedwoodClient; client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))... then call client.chat.create(prompt=...)
02:36 Alex: is there a streaming example? we need tokens as they stream for UX.
02:40 Samira: yes we have streaming bindings in both py and ts. the py example uses async for chunk in client.chat.stream(...): print(chunk.text) — sometimes the auto-transcript munges the await but it's standard async iteration.
02:55 Priya: any gotchas around proxies or corporate egress? we route traffic through a central egress host.
03:00 Samira: you can configure the SDK to use an HTTP proxy; in our Private deployments the control plane is in-vpc so egress stays internal. for hosted you'll need to allow outbound to our public endpoints or use Private Link where available.

03:20 Jordan: let's talk credentials for CI. Samira, show the example GH Actions snippet.
03:25 Samira: yep — uses secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY, we recommend creating a low-privilege key for CI with a token limit and rotation schedule. also recommend storing the key encrypted in your vault, not in repo. note: the default key created from console has broad scopes; you can scope by model and route to reduce blast radius.
03:50 Miguel: can we restrict per-route tokens? our compliance wants least privilege.
03:55 Samira: yes you can create tokens scoped to specific routes and models and also set rate limits and TTLs. that's in the API Keys section.

04:15 Samira: switching to TypeScript — npm install @redwood/sdk then const client = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }) — example uses env vars and dotenv in local dev.
04:32 Alex: any guidance for monorepo multi-env — dev, staging, prod keys?
04:36 Samira: we recommend separate projects/environments in the console, with distinct keys and quotas. use service accounts for CI and RBAC to limit access.

04:50 Jordan: let's talk about Optimize and batching. for chat-heavy UX our Optimize module suggests batching small requests and enabling KV/prefix cache for repeated prompts.
05:03 Samira: we ran a similar workload with 1k concurrent users — batching gave ~20% token cost reduction but we had to tune latency SLOs. Optimize gives quantization recommendations if you want to run on Dedicated to save cost, but watch quality shifts.
05:22 Priya: how do you detect quality regressions after quantization or model swaps?
05:28 Samira: we tie evals to prompt sets and auto-alert on perplexity or metric drift; there's a canary rollout where a small percentage uses the quantized model and we compare outputs. we'll show you the configs.

05:45 Jordan: security folks usually ask about logs and retention. hosted keeps audit logs and you can export to your SIEM; Dedicated/Private can ship logs to your S3 or syslog.
05:58 Miguel: retention requirements: can we set short retention for PII?
06:02 Samira: yes, retention policies per project, and redaction rules for specific fields. in Private you have full control.

06:15 Priya: okay concrete ask — can you provision a sandbox and a demo key we can give to two engineers? we want to run an end-to-end integration with our pipeline.
06:22 Samira: i'll provision solstice-poc-demo and add Priya and Alex. Jordan i'll email the invite and the onboarding doc with python/ts snippets.
06:30 Jordan: i'll also include the security questionnaire and SOC2. Miguel, you mentioned private deployment questions. could you bullet those and send back?
06:36 Miguel: sure i'll send a short list by EoW.

06:50 Priya: latency — our SLO is 150ms 95p for short prompts. can you achieve that on hosted?
06:56 Samira: depends on model and sequence length. for short prompts we can hit <100ms on dedicated avx-optimized instances. hosted can be close but we'd recommend a dedicated pool for strict SLOs. we'll propose two profiles: hosted pilot, and a Dedicated baseline with GPU class and batching settings.
07:18 Alex: what about on-prem? we have customers that want air-gapped.
07:22 Samira: Private on-prem package is available, though it's a heavier integration — we provide an air-gapped bundle and onsite installation guidance. that ties into your compliance asks.

07:38 Jordan: objections — cost vs latency tradeoff is common. we'll show cost model in the proposal and highlight Optimize levers — quantization, batching, prefix caching — to balance.
07:50 Priya: are there any third-party competitors you'll be comparing against from our side?
07:54 Jordan: some teams look at Anthropic or self-hosting. we've got benchmark sheets showing perf/cost for typical workloads; i'll share that.

08:10 Samira: demo wrap-up — quick look at logs in the console, tracing per-request, token-level cost view. then a route-level dashboard that surfaces latency and error breakdowns.
08:25 Jordan: OK let's recap next steps — Jordan to send security + SOC2 + POC pricing; Samira to provision sandbox and keys; Solstice to run a bench and circle back with perf numbers; Miguel to share private deployment Qs.

08:40 Priya: sounds good. one last minor question: will the SDK change function signatures frequently? we want stable CI.
08:45 Samira: semver and deprecation policy — we publish SDK changelogs and give a deprecation window. breaking changes are rare and we provide migration guides.

08:55 Alex: thanks everyone — we'll try to hit the bench by Jan 2.
09:00 Jordan: great, thanks all. we'll follow up with invites and docs. end recording.
